key_insight: Under identical controlled conditions, the continuous-variable (CV) quantum head consistently outperforms the discrete-variable (DV) head for wafer-map defect classification, indicating the CV circuit is better suited to this spatially structured task.
engineering_relevance: For semiconductor yield screening, this suggests CV quantum neural network layers may be more promising than DV layers when defect patterns require fine spatial discrimination, especially as a plug-in head on a shared classical backbone.
method: Shared convolutional backbone (~4.3M parameters) for all models
Interchangeable heads: classical dense, CV-QNN, or DV-QNN
Quantum heads scaled at 3, 4, and 8 qumodes/qubits
evidence_signal: On WM-811K eight-class wafer-map classification, the CV head at four qumodes reached 79.7 ± 1.8% accuracy versus 61.6 ± 1.4% for DV, and CV recall on Edge-Loc was 0.66 ± 0.06 while DV was ≤0.05 at all sizes.
watch_item: Both quantum heads still trail the classical baseline and the reported advantage depends on the chosen low Fock cutoff and controlled setup, so hardware noise and scaling could change the ranking.
paper_title: Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification
